core_principles: Keep the shoulder joint fixed and stable during the curl to ensure the elbow joint experiences the primary reaction moment and displacement.
Isolate the movement to the elbow joint to properly target the biceps brachii muscle and tendon.
common_mistakes: Allowing excessive displacement or movement at the shoulder joint instead of keeping it fixed.
specific_findings: The biceps curl movement was analyzed using 6 kg and 10.7 kg dumbbells.
The shoulder joint was regarded as fixed during the simulation due to observing only a small displacement.
The biceps brachii model used a tendon length (Lt) of 0.0625 m and a total muscle length (Lm) of 0.312 m.
Muscle material properties were defined with a density of 1056 kg/m3, Poisson's ratio of 0.4, and Young's modulus of 1.162·106 Pa.
Tendon material properties were defined with a density of 1670 kg/m3, Poisson's ratio of 0.497, and Young's modulus of 1.6·106 Pa.

core_principles: Start the movement with the elbow joint in full extension.
Flex the forearm until the dumbbells reach the top of the shoulders.
Return the arms to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Keep the elbows close to the body throughout the entire movement.
common_mistakes: Failing to start the movement from full elbow extension.
Allowing the elbows to drift away from the body during the curl.
specific_findings: Increasing the dumbbell load by 78.3% (from 6 kg to 10.7 kg) resulted in an elbow peak moment increase of only 57.7%.
With a 78.3% load increase, the rate of increase of peak muscle force of the biceps brachii was 38.3%.
The rate of increase of maximum strain and maximum stress under this load increase was 44.4% and 37.3%, respectively.
Increasing the dumbbell load does not increase the muscle force at the same rate.

core_principles: The mechanical response of the biceps brachii does not scale linearly with increased dumbbell load.
The muscle moment arm distance changes dynamically throughout the range of motion of a dumbbell curl, which directly influences the joint moment and muscle force.
Increasing the external load results in a disproportionately lower increase in peak muscle force due to the changing moment arm and non-linear muscle-tendon properties.
specific_findings: Peak joint moment was 18.88 Nm with a 6 kg dumbbell and 29.78 Nm with a 10.7 kg dumbbell (a 57.7% increase).
Peak muscle force was 645.66 N with a 6 kg dumbbell and 893.04 N with a 10.7 kg dumbbell (a 38.3% increase).
Maximum strain was 4.44 mm/mm with a 6 kg dumbbell and 6.42 mm/mm with a 10.7 kg dumbbell (a 37.3% increase).
Mean maximum stress (σmax) was 4.85 MPa with a 6 kg dumbbell and 7.46 MPa with a 10.7 kg dumbbell.
Peak maximum stress (σmax) was 7.76 MPa with a 6 kg dumbbell and 10.66 MPa with a 10.7 kg dumbbell (a 44.4% increase in maximum stress).
